gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-new-tv-trai.excerpt: GTA 6 's marketing push is ramping up substantially, and that includes with TV commercials. Eagled-eyes fans have discovered that the new GTA 6 TV spots actually contain some extended sequences, but just barely. For starters, a 30-second TV spot cuts out the steamy shower scenes with Jason and Lucia from the launch trailer . While the shower scenes are gone in this edit, the new TV spot has a slightly longer shots of an airplane sequence and another with Jason and Lucia standing next to their car. Jason playfully nudges Lucia, and in the TV spot, she nearly topples to the ground. The Xbox logo was also removed, presumably due to Rockstar's reported promotional deal with Sony. You can check out the comparison below ( via IGN ). https://twitter.com/GTAVI_Countdown/status/2112897438885245268 A 90-second version, meanwhile, includes the shower scenes, along with the slightly longer sequences seen in the 30-second version. If you saw these TV spots recently, you might not have even noticed any of these changes, but GTA 6 fan accounts are extremely dedicated and never miss anything. https://twitter.com/mnm345x/status/2113001090245664971 GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and, yes, Xbox Series X|S, even though the TV ads for the game don't tell you that. Rockstar's marketing push for the game also includes real-life Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell restaurants where you can buy GTA-branded food . In other GTA 6 news, it was recently reported that preorders are pacing significantly ahead of any other big AAA game of the past five years . Obviously that's no surprise, given GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest game release ever, and it could generate $2 billion before it even launches.

gamespot.com/articles/im-getting-very-wo.title: I’m Getting Very Worried About Skate Following EA Layoffs
gamespot.com/articles/im-getting-very-wo.excerpt: Publisher Electronic Arts recently slashed 400 roles across its company , which resulted in the shuttering of legendary RPG studio BioWare . But also impacted by the layoffs was Skate developer Full Circle, and now I'm growing increasingly worried about the future of a franchise I waited so long to make a comeback. Part of EA's latest round of layoffs on October 21 included cutting an unspecified number of staffers to create a "very clear roadmap" that leads to a "healthier and more sustainable business." Then, as VGC noted on the same day , "many" of the developers at Full Circle are gone. This includes artists Brendan Vermeltfoort and Will Granda, seasonal creative director John Epler, and senior designers Adam Martinazzi and David Milne--all of whom posted the unfortunate news on LinkedIn. It's always a bummer when talented developers lose their jobs at the hands of corporate greed, but this one stings for me personally. As a big Skate girlie, I was so stoked for the franchise to make a comeback, and even more stoked to get my hands on the game in September 2025. It's had its stumbles, to be sure. Season 2 was light on new content. Season 3 introduced a new map ... that was locked behind a paywall. Season 4 gave us an empty stadium ... that was also locked behind a paywall. But despite bailing on every trick, you could see Full Circle getting closer to landing at each attempt. gamespot.com/articles/it-isnt-debra-wils.title: It Isn’t Debra Wilson’s Fault She’s In Everything
gamespot.com/articles/it-isnt-debra-wils.excerpt: Debra Wilson’s voice, one of the most recognizable in video games, carries a singular authority. It’s a sound that’s propped up special agents, presidents, military commanders, dragons, demons, and Jedi masters. But despite her incredible range--Wolfenstein cutscene director Tom Keegan calls her "his muse" because he loves to work with her so much--she’s also one of gaming's most recognizable faces. Game developers often scan her and build characters around her commanding presence, individuality, and unmistakable aura. It’s a blessing and a curse for an actor who wants to inhabit characters. Wilson has voiced main characters in over 100 different games, but there is also at least a double-digit number of games in which the creators have used her physical likeness, as well. "I don’t necessarily dig it," Wilson told GameSpot in an exclusive interview. "Because I might as well be doing it on camera. It's hard to suspend your disbelief. There are people who are like, ‘Oh my God, she's in every f***ing game. What the f***?’ And there are other people like, ‘I am sick of looking at her face because I just want to play the game and not think of Debra Wilson.’" Recently, Wilson’s prominence in games was parodied in Focus M , an internet video poking fun at AAA game design. The video sees Mario running around a horrifically generic fan-made Unreal Engine-style world, quipping and being guided by a voice on the radio. The big reveal at the end shows Wilson in her home booth, as the voice behind Toadsworth. While it suggests she’s in on the joke, unfortunately--like her Destiny 2 farewell video --it just came in as a request on Cameo, a service where fans pay actors to record lines in character. She’d never seen the video until I showed it to her, though she said she loved it. gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-is-kee.title: WoW: Forever Is Keeping Its Secrets Close To The Chest
gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-is-kee.excerpt: World of Warcraft: Forever players may have searched its beta with a fine-toothed comb, but Blizzard said there are still plenty of secrets waiting to be found come launch and beyond. In a new WoW: Forever Podcast dedicated to the end of the beta, Blizzard made clear it's keeping many of the game's surprises close to its chest. Senior game designer Josh Greenfield said Blizzard had disabled some items and secrets for the beta. He gave an example of a new torch item that was originally turned off for the beta's first week, but later enabled to test out Forever's new lighting and fog tech. He said players can expect more of those types of surprises. "There's definitely some secrets and stuff that we had turned off," Greenfield said when asked about still to be discovered secrets in the level 1-30 zones. "There's going to be things to discover that we didn't surface, suffice to say that." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uOlxa3xvNq4 Forever's beta had a maximum level of 30, meaning there is still a huge chunk of the game, including new zones, quests, dungeons, and raids, players haven't fully explored yet. When asked about items like a newly discovered sword in the beta that could potentially enable new playstyles, like a melee-focused "Battle Mage", Greenfield opted not to elaborate further. "It's hard to talk about secret stuff," Greenfield said. "It's secret, right? We want people to find it. There's some really, really, really cool, and really, really, really well-buried stuff out there that's probably going to take people a long time to find. If we tip our hats to it too much, it's just going to take the fun away." Unlike in past WoW releases, most of the items on Forever's beta were hidden from dataminers using a new system that hides an item's name and stats until it's discovered by the community. gamespot.com/articles/the-leaked-mass-ef.title: The Leaked Mass Effect 5 Trailer Is Absolutely Heartbreaking
gamespot.com/articles/the-leaked-mass-ef.excerpt: After hearing the disappointing news that EA has shuttered BioWare , putting an end to two of my favorite RPG franchises— Mass Effect and Dragon Age —I have been, like so many other players, feeling pretty bummed out. But I consoled myself with the fact that, given the environment at BioWare in recent years, the now-canceled Mass Effect 5 probably wouldn't be that good anyway. Like many players, I enjoyed the Mass Effect trilogy, but felt that Mass Effect: Andromeda fell short. Similarly, BioWare's other recent titles— Anthem and Dragon Age: The Veilguard —struggled with messy development cycles marked by frequent changes in direction, mixed messages from higher-ups at EA, constant staff turnover, and other issues that ultimately led to an underwhelming gaming experience. After playing Veilguard, which felt nothing like the Dragon Age games I had grown to love, my hopes weren't too high for Mass Effect 5. The news of its cancellation (and BioWare's subsequent shutdown) was a huge bummer, though I'd rather Mass Effect go out on a relatively high note than see it get the Veilguard treatment. But then I saw the trailer. Uploaded to Reddit earlier today, the trailer has not been verified as real by BioWare, but it doesn't appear to bear any hallmarks of generative AI, and a short message before the trailer begins implies it was planned to debut at a later date—perhaps N7 Day, or The Game Awards. "The following is in-engine footage from our small team," reads the text displayed before the trailer begins. "It uses our pre-production assets." What follows is one of the most exciting game trailers I've seen in years. We learn the name of the game—Mass Effect: Universe—and meet the male version of its protagonist (though given the history of the franchise, it's likely players would have been able to play as whatever gender they prefer). gamespot.com/articles/why-people-think-v.title: Why People Think Valve Just Accidentally Confirmed Half-Life 3
gamespot.com/articles/why-people-think-v.excerpt: People online are going wild thinking that Valve may have accidentally revealed the existence of a new Half-Life game after a developer mentioned a project referred to as "HLX." Speaking at the Game Sound Con event , Valve sound designer Mike Morasky was discussing how Valve's games utilize high dynamic range (HDR) audio systems. He specifically called out how upcoming Valve game Deadlock has its own version of HDR and so does a project called HLX. Another Valve developer sitting next to Morasky says to him immediately after, "Nice work," seemingly in reference to how Morasky might have spoken out of turn here by mentioning HLX. You can also see the other Valve developer saying to Morasky, "Good job, you only said HLX once." https://twitter.com/gabefollower/status/2113342715756978245 Morasky is a Valve veteran, having worked on the sound and music for games like Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, Portal 2, Half-Life: Alyx, and Counter-Strike 2. Outside of games, he worked on visual effects for Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings movies and The Matrix trilogy. He was a member of the band Steel Pole Bath Tab. A while back, a datamining effort found references to something called HLX, and some think it's a new Half-Life game, or possibly the fabled Half-Life 3 . For what it's worth, it's become something of an annual tradition for people to get excited about the smallest possible evidence of a new Half-Life , only to be disappointed when nothing gets announced. The Half-Life franchise has a dedicated fanbase and the franchise has major cache, so it wouldn't be surprising to see Valve return to the series again after 2020's VR game Half-Life: Alyx . That was GameSpot's Game of the Year that year.

gamespot.com/articles/gears-of-war-e-day.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Cost Half A Billion To Make, Apparently
gamespot.com/articles/gears-of-war-e-day.excerpt: Multiple new reports claim that the budget for Gears of War: E-Day was $500 million. Both Kotaku and Chris Dring of The Game Business reported today, with Kotaku's report saying the number does not include marketing costs. Jez Corden of Windows Central added that the $500 million figure is not wrong, but his own sources aren't able to say definitively if that number covers the game's budget alone, or the game's budget plus additional costs related to running the development studio, The Coalition. https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Bn4cMZamNA4 Whatever the case, the consensus seems to be that E-Day was an expensive game to produce, and the game's early sales results do not seem very impressive. The game reportedly sold 230,000 copies across Xbox and PC , but that doesn't tell the whole story since the game is included with Xbox Game Pass . Further data shows that the game reached nearly 2 million people out of the gate, and that number is sure to grow over time. Game Pass is a juggernaut for Microsoft and Xbox, with its recurring revenue from subscriptions generating almost $5 billion annually based on the latest data. A $500 million development budget for E-Day would represent 10% of that annual revenue from Game Pass. Industry expert Mike Futter reacted to Kotaku's report about E-Day's $500 million budget, saying, "Exclusivity on console games simply does not make sense right now," even if the development budget was half of that. E-Day was expected to release on PS5, and Microsoft's own presentational materials showed that , but the game was not released on Sony's console. According to reports, Microsoft canceled a PS5 edition at the last minute, with others saying E-Day was being sent out to die on purpose . GameSpot has contacted Xbox seeking comment about E-Day's reported budget. gamespot.com/articles/ea-could-sell-biow.title: EA Could Sell BioWare’s IP As It Looks To Tackle Its Massive Debt, Former Studio Boss Says
gamespot.com/articles/ea-could-sell-biow.excerpt: It's a grim week for developers and fans, with EA announcing that it is shutting down Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio BioWare. EA said that after deciding not to pursue development on a new Mass Effect, it would shut down the studio as part of company-wide restructuring plans that will result in roughly 400 employees being let go. But should EA sit on the IP that BioWare was responsible for and let it gather dust? Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah has suggested they could go up for sale as it works off some of its $55 billion debt. "Remember BioWare, 100% owned by EA," Darrah said on his YouTube channel. “EA owns all the IP. They own Dragon Age, they own Mass Effect, they own Jade Empire. That doesn’t change the situation. Now, here’s nobody working on a game, or games, within the EA organization, and chances are there never will be, which might make them more likely to sell off those IP. But it might also make them more likely to just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault. I think we still are going to have to wait a little bit before we see if EA has any interest in selling off some of its dormant IP. Right now, they seem to be in cost-control mode. They might start into a revenue-generation mode where selling IP might be more desirable." https://youtu.be/2T8KlKPa2Y0 Earlier this year, former Dragon Age lead writer David Gaider also spoke about the franchise and said he believed it was dead after the poor commercial performance of Dragon Age: The Veilguard. BioWare's last game failed to meet EA's expectations, and mass layoffs at BioWare eventually left only a core team to focus on the next Mass Effect game . While EA doesn't have anyone internally to work on a game based on a BioWare IP, that doesn't mean it can't look outward to find a studio to handle work on a new Mass Effect or Jade Empire--if it chooses to. gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-moder.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Tips For Multiplayer
gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-moder.excerpt: We went hands-on with Modern Warfare 4 early, and while it will feel familiar to many Call of Duty veterans, Infinity Ward has updated some of the movement mechanics and features from recent years. In this guide, we'll provide some of the best tips to help you score wins in multiplayer when Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23. Practice the new movement Modern Warfare 4 overhauls the movement from the last two years of Treyarch's Black Ops games. This game strips away the fancy omnimovement, but Infinity Ward has reworked the mantling system, refined the sliding mechanic, and added a way to climb up pipes. The best way to get practice with Modern Warfare 4's movement system is to play the game's new mobility course, which is found in the multiplayer playlist menu. It includes a series of three difficulties, including tutorials for beginners, intermediate, and experts. There are rewards for completing the mobility course as well. Without omnimovement, double jumps into windows and other high places are no longer possible. However, you can climb up pipes to reach otherwise inaccessible areas. These specific pipes are copper in color and stand out fairly easily. These are found on standard multiplayer maps, Kill Block, and even Modern Warfare 4's Zodiac map for Warzone. Hipfire is your friend Infinity Ward removed bloom from guns this year, which is a mechanic that previously caused bullet spread when firing from the hip, meaning some bullets did not hit their target. Hipfiring is more accurate in Modern Warfare 4, so you don't always need to aim down sights with your gun. If someone is sliding at you from around a corner, or perhaps you just find yourself in a close-range engagement. Don't waste time aiming. Just hipfire your gun. Adjust your settings Modern Warfare 4 has plenty of customization and accessibility settings. gamespot.com/articles/how-will-gas-and-r.title: How Will Gas And Refueling Work In GTA 6?
gamespot.com/articles/how-will-gas-and-r.excerpt: As more Grand Theft Auto 6 previews roll out, one topic seems to be proving pretty controversial among fans--the realistic need to refuel your vehicle. Some players think it's a little egregious of Rockstar to force you to hunt down gasoline, while others consider that because of the game's other realistic mechanisms--like relationships , working out, and escaping the police --that needing to refuel should have been introduced to the franchise a long while back. While the details aren't concrete right now, we know there will be at least two types of cars--ones that need gasoline and electric vehicles. There may be some hybrid vehicles, but it hasn't been confirmed just yet. You'll have to charge electric cars, of course, but we know more about how fueling a vehicle works. It seems to be a quick time event (QTE) that lasts around 10 seconds. You'll have to hold the gas pump, hold R2 or RB, and pump gas until the car is full. However, there's more of a risk if you've stolen a car--if you want to get away but you have to take a detour to a gas station because you're running out of fuel, it will be less than ideal. That's made even more difficult if you're sporting a Wanted level for stealing it in the first place. This will change the way we behave with our vehicles throughout the entire game. It seems like Rockstar wants you to care about the vehicle you have, rather than in previous instalments where there was no incentive to look after your car. You'd just see a new vehicle, ditch your current one, and steal that instead. If you've just spent some hard-earned cash on filling it with gas so that it's a reliable getaway vehicle, you're going to be far less likely to ditch it. Filling a car with gas has existed basically since cars have been in games, prominently in racing games where you'd have to pull over to refuel, or more recently in simulation games like My Summer Car, The Long Drive, and more. gamespot.com/articles/your-mind-is-playi.title: Your Mind Is Playing Tricks On You: Why You Hear What You Want To Hear In Control Resonant
gamespot.com/articles/your-mind-is-playi.excerpt: Control Resonant is delightfully weird: a sequel that isn't afraid to fly its freak flag as it pits you against all manner of supernatural phenomena wreaking havoc on Manhattan. But between bosses that resemble Francis Bacon-inspired nightmare fuel and other spooky occurrences, The Board is undoubtedly the scene-stealer of Control Resonant--and that's without you even seeing them! The Board is louder than ever as it accompanies Dylan Faden in Remedy's new game, seemingly trapped in the powerful shape-shifting artifact that he uses to smash his way through The Hiss and The Patterning. A successful run elicits booming words of encouragement/motivation/incentive from the paranatural entities that make up The Board, each interaction being the equivalent of a shotgun blast of indecipherable bass that'll tickle your audio receptors. So what goes into designing and developing a "character" like The Board? A surprising amount of technical wizardry and experimentation, as Lucas Pierrot, audio lead on Control Resonant, explained. The Board is right here, and you get to experience the full council Compared to Control, The Board's audio identity is very different. Gone are the sounds of telephonic voices, replaced with something more uniquely alien and commanding. Why the change? As Pierrot explained, The Board spoke to players through a hotline in Control, but in Control Resonant, they have a direct line of communication to Dylan, and by extension, the player. "From an audio perspective, the main shift is now [that] The Board is speaking directly into Dylan’s mind, in full definition," Pierrot said. "In the original Control, the board talks through the hotline, an old phone connecting you to a remote mysterious place, hence the static and muffled audio. Here there are no filters anymore. gamespot.com/articles/in-a-biddy-blas-of.title: In A (Biddy) Blas Of Glory: How Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Smallest Racer Made Such A Huge Impact
gamespot.com/articles/in-a-biddy-blas-of.excerpt: Biddy Blas could probably use a booster cushion on his speeder to see more clearly over its handlebars, but he hasn't needed any sort of booster to make a massive impression on the internet. This squat, reptilian nuisance from Star Wars: Galactic Racer has overtaken social media algorithms with a ceaseless flood of fan-made skits, memes, and thirst traps. Blas and his shrill Huttese barks have acted almost as unexpected marketing for the game, seemingly having a greater reach and impact than the smattering of high review scores . And like a podracer barreling down the Mos Espa Raceway, it has all come at Richard Summers-Calvert, the voice behind the Crocin racer, incredibly quickly . "I knew we had created something special," Summers-Calvert told GameSpot. "I knew we created something people would really enjoy and [Blas] was going to be really irritating. And I remember posting on my Instagram Stories [something vague] like, ‘I just had a really lovely session. Can’t wait for you all to see it.’ And that post popped up again recently, and I really did feel great that day going home. And I was like, ‘We’ve definitely done something cool.’ I had no idea it would be this successful and this positive." Similarly struck by this success is Galactic Racer's music and narrative director, Nathaniel Daw, who was quick to recall the initial, eye-opening recording sessions with Summers-Calvert. According to Daw, the Star Wars-free early scripts--which were filled with all sorts of codenames meant to obfuscate what title voice actors were actually reading for--didn’t give Summers-Calvert much to go on other than this mystery character having a tiny stature that betrayed his large ego. And despite the opaqueness, the muscular, red-headed actor took a bold swing. "About halfway through, he just lets out this incredible laugh," recalled Daw in an interview with GameSpot. gamespot.com/articles/arkane-lyon-could-.title: Arkane Lyon Could Be Shut Down Within Weeks As Deadline To Find A Buyer Looms
gamespot.com/articles/arkane-lyon-could-.excerpt: It might be the end of the road for Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon, as a new report says that the studio has until November 13 to find a buyer or face closure. Le Monde reported that while Microsoft had followed the procedure as laid out in Florange Law--French legislation that requires Microsoft to spend at least three months searching for a buyer for Arkane Lyon--negotiations were going "badly," and worker unions are currently attempting to buy more time to save jobs at the studio, which is currently still working on Marvel's Blade. The report says "several forms of takeover" are being considered, but the union's plans could include re-employing affected staff at other Xbox studios or taking Microsoft to court. According to IGN , development on Marvel's Blade was still on track for a new reveal in early 2027, followed by a Q4 2027 release. The game was originally revealed in December 2023 , but aside from a handful of concept art images since then, nothing else has been shown. Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier also corroborated reports of "multiple paths" being explored and that he'd be surprised if the studio is shut down. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wB9ye56mSfk If Arkane Lyon is facing closure, it'll be the end of a studio that has been around for 27 years. Its first game was Arx Fatalis in 2002, and it followed that up with the release of Dark Messiah of Might and Magic (2006) and KarmaStar (2009). Since the 2010s, the studio has pumped out several hits like the Dishonored games and Deathloop. The Texas-based studio that it operated, Arkane Austin, was established in 2006, but following the release of the critically panned Redfall in 2023, it was shut down in 2024 . Arkane Lyon's departure from the Xbox Games Studio portfolio was announced earlier this year, alongside Double Fine Productions, Compulsion Games, Undead Labs, and Ninja Theory. gamespot.com/articles/rideshare-stimulat.title: Rideshare Stimulator’s Biggest Problem Isn’t AI, It’s That The Game Just Isn’t Very Good
gamespot.com/articles/rideshare-stimulat.excerpt: Saber Interactive's driving game Rideshare Stimulator has already made headlines for all the wrong reasons. But while its use of AI and the allegations from a former writer have attracted plenty of attention, Rideshare Stimulator has a far more fundamental problem to overcome: being an enjoyable game to play. You're put in the driver's seat of a rideshare business that you co-own with your buddy, Tim. You'll have to pick up a variety of passengers, navigate traffic (and adhere to the usual rules of the road) and earn enough money to keep the business running. It has the potential to be a pretty fun gameplay loop, especially when there's an ongoing side mission to restore an old sports car housed in your garage. Unfortunately, the more Rideshare Stimulator attempts to simulate the realities of the job, the less appealing it becomes. https://youtu.be/lQxBAE1tE8g After Rideshare Stimulator was announced, it almost immediately began drawing criticism after former lead writer Stella Sacco alleged that Saber Interactive had replaced her with AI-generated writing midway through development. Stacco claimed that she was removed from the project and that AI was used to write the remaining text, including material intended for future updates. Saber disputed her account, insisting that neither it nor developer Unigine had replaced writers with AI. The company maintained that the actual storyline for the game was written by humans, but acknowledged that generative AI would be used in an experimental free-ride mode featuring an endless supply of passenger interactions. The dispute escalated when Saber CEO Matthew Karch responded publicly to Sacco's claims. His comments included a personal attack on the former writer, suggesting that he would have been happy to replace her with AI in retrospect. gamespot.com/articles/battlefield-6-repo.title: Battlefield 6 Reportedly Cancels Mass Effect Collab In Wake Of BioWare Closure
gamespot.com/articles/battlefield-6-repo.excerpt: Battlefield Studios is reportedly cancelling plans for a Mass Effect collaboration in Battlefield 6 in the wake of EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the next game in the sci-fi series . Fans discovered various Mass Effect-themed cosmetics in Battlefield 6's files, with many speculating that they would be released in November, tied to the Mass Effect N7 Day holiday on November 7. Those cosmetics, which included Mass Effect-themed weapon charms and patches, have seemingly now been removed from Battlefield 6's in-game store prior to their general availability ( via Kotaku ). https://www.reddit.com/r/LowSodiumBattlefield/comments/1xcmb3o/the_seemingly_planned_bf6_x_mass_effect_pack_is/?utm_source=embedv2&utm_medium=post_embed&utm_content=post_title&embed_host_url=https%3A%2F%2Fkotaku.com%2Fbattlefield-6-mass-effect-cosmetics-n7-day-store-2000749091 If these Mass Effect-themed cosmetics were indeed real, getting yanked only makes sense, considering the blowback EA and Battlefield Studios would have faced for hawking new items based on a franchise that it just killed off. While this Mass Effect collab might not be going ahead, Battlefield 6 is currently hosting a crossover event with Dead Space . It might make financial sense to close BioWare and cancel the Mass Effect series, but fans are upset about the 30-year studio that blazed a trail for queer representation in games closing up shop. The closure of BioWare comes after EA was taken private by an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Due to the structuring of the deal as a leveraged buyout, EA is on the hook for a lot of debt, and there will likely be more layoffs and pain for the people working at EA in the time ahead.

The first is just tapping your thumb with each finger on the same hand, which as a personal aside, can be a good mindfulness technique, too. The next finger drill sees you spreading your hand out and making a five, then turning that into a fist with your thumb on the outside. Our added suggestion is to do spirit fingers between fists to look as ridiculous as possible. Last but not least, Hope recommends finger pushups, where you "press the fingertips of both hands on the floor and push pressure into your fingers," according to the press release. PureGym advises people to do these exercises 10 times each, as well as after a long session with GTA VI. "We warm up before a run or a gym session, so why not before a long gaming session? Your thumbs and hands are doing the heavy lifting, and the rest of your body is barely moving," Hope said. It didn’t have the fun or the charm of the classic games in the series, and while the world was waiting for GTA 6, it should’ve been the lightning-in-a-bottle moment to reignite the love for the dormant Saints. While it didn’t work out, Saints Row: The Third Remastered is still a classic, and you should buy it while you wait for the Grand Theft Auto 6 release date to roll around, especially when it’s under $5. Before GTA V took the world by storm, Saints Row: The Third blew my mind. It had the same “running a gang” vibe that the Grand Theft Auto games delivered, but with a focus on adding a zany, whimsical charm to what should’ve been serious. You play as a custom character known as The Boss, who lands in Steelport and is forced to deal with the Syndicate and three of its divisions, taking over the city in the Saints’ name. Comparing it to the iconic GTA series is a bit unfair in some ways. While they’re both open-world games focused on committing crimes, and both are fairly satirical, Saints Row: The Third removes the delicate balance that GTA strives for in favor of going absolutely bonkers in many cases. The opening has the Saints starring in a movie about themselves, for example. It’s not exactly on the nose so much as it is punching you square in the face. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_j5FAX8nEy8&pp=ygUnc2FpbnRzIHJvdyB0aGUgdGhpcmQgcmVtYXN0ZXJlZCB0cmFpbGVy However, that makes it unique and distinct enough that you won’t get burnt out while waiting for Grand Theft Auto VI. The third-person action leans more toward the outlandish than the realistic, yet the narrative still focuses on more serious themes, making the entire game feel like its own thing. It’s not as bombastic as the fourth entry, with world-ending threats and superpowers, but it’s still fun without being overly cringe. gamespot.com/articles/xbox-wanted-a-garg.title: Xbox Wanted A Gargantuan Paycheck To Partner With Netflix On TV And Movies
gamespot.com/articles/xbox-wanted-a-garg.excerpt: Video game adaptations are all the rage right now, with movie and TV projects in various stages of development, and Netflix is looking to strike while the proverbial IP iron is hot. The streaming giant already has a deal in place with Microsoft to develop a Gears of War movie , and it's looking to grab more Xbox IP to build new franchises. The only problem? Microsoft's price tag was reportedly quite a bit more than Netflix was willing to pay. That's according to entertainment journalist Matthew Belloni, who wrote in a Puck News report that Netflix had offered Microsoft $500 million for seven years to exclusively license Xbox titles for film and TV. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and the brand's business affairs team countered by demanding $800 million, prompting Netflix to rescind the offer. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzqGbNaOROA While Netflix has declined to comment on the report, Xbox told Belloni it had received "record-breaking interest" in its IP and still values Netflix as a partner on upcoming projects. Belloni added that Xbox is now "pursuing smaller deals with more partners," like the Diablo animated series under development at Netflix, another season of Fallout at Prime Video, the Call of Duty movie at Paramount, and a sequel to A Minecraft Movie at Warner Bros. Pictures. Xbox is also expanding its multimedia ambitions; earlier this month, it announced Xbox XP . This new arm of the company, devoted to movies, TV, merchandise, theme parks, and live events, will be headed by Lucasfilm veteran Kayleen Walters. Xbox Pictures is one of its subdivisions, and it'll develop film and television projects, as well as other forms of "linear storytelling" using Xbox IP.

gamespot.com/articles/cancelling-mass-ef.title: Cancelling Mass Effect And Closing BioWare Was An Obvious Thing For EA To Do, Experts Say
gamespot.com/articles/cancelling-mass-ef.excerpt: Electronic Arts just confirmed a major shakeup that included the closure of BioWare and cancellation of its upcoming Mass Effect game. Closing the studio and cancelling the project was a horrible thing for the people who worked there and fans who enjoy BioWare games and were looking forward to the next Mass Effect . But taking that action was no surprise whatsoever from a business sense. Video game analyst Joost Van Dreunen told IGN that EA needed to make drastic cuts to service the $18 billion in debt that it has taken on due to the leveraged structure of its sale to Saudi Arabia's PIF, Silver Lake, and Affinity. Interest payments alone on that debt are about $1.8 billion annually, which exceeds how much money EA makes in annual EBITDA ($1.5 billion). Van Dreunen said BioWare getting shut down was "entirely predictable and precisely what a leveraged buyout looks like once the deal closes." "In that context, a 50-person team working on a game that is years from launch is the easiest line to cut, regardless of its legacy,” van Dreunen said. Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere Analysis, meanwhile, said the closure of BioWare is "emotive"  for people who loved BioWare and its 30-year legacy of making popular and well-liked RPGs, but the math just didn't math. Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet sales expectations , and Mass Effect: Andromeda and Anthem were commercial disappointments, too. This contributed to an environment where EA management would look to kill the studio outright. He said EA was likely already considering big changes for BioWare prior to the acquisition even closing. “Unfortunately, the studio’s recent big-budget releases have not performed well enough commercially," he said. gamespot.com/articles/bioware-is-no-more.title: BioWare Is No More, But Its Impact On Queer Representation In Video Games Will Live On Forever
gamespot.com/articles/bioware-is-no-more.excerpt: BioWare was shuttered by Electronic Arts earlier this week , resulting in 50 or so people losing their jobs and the upcoming Mass Effect 5 being cancelled. While the studio’s last decade of struggles have been frequently documented as games like Mass Effect Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to live up to expectations, there nevertheless existed an optimism among fans that the magic would return. Much of this fainthearted hope rested on Mass Effect 5, a game many believed would right the studio's wrongs and pull this architect of modern RPGs away from the brink of oblivion. But I was wrong. Now BioWare is no more, and it breaks my heart. Like millions of others, I grew up with Mass Effect and Dragon Age : Origins and view them as magnificent achievements, the likes of which we might never see in video games again. They were a selection of bold and ambitious adventures that introduced us to larger-than-life worlds and extraordinary characters that would quickly cement themselves into legend. They each gave players the freedom to be themselves by creating avatars who represented who they wanted to be in reality. While there were several obstacles to conquer along the way, BioWare spearheaded LGBTQ+ representation in video games like few others before it as bigotry was pushed aside in favor of progress. As BioWare is lowered into the grave, I have already seen countless people share how this beloved studio helped not only shape their tastes in art and storytelling, but also gave them the building blocks required to assemble their own identities. When I first created a female version of Commander Shepard and fell in love with Liara T'Soni aboard the Normandy as a closeted kid, I had no idea it might be the first sign of who I truly was. But now that decades have passed and I find myself on that queer journey--I can’t thank BioWare enough for paving the way. gamespot.com/articles/control-resonant-u.title: Control Resonant’s Unsettling Board Dialogue Is Carefully Crafted Gibberish
gamespot.com/articles/control-resonant-u.excerpt: Just what is The Board in Control Resonant ? While we still have plenty of questions about the otherworldly entity that accompanies players on their trip across Manhattan, one thing we do know is that it's loud, incomprehensible, and you can't understand what it's saying without subtitles. Some players are convinced The Board is saying something specific if you listen closely, but according to developer Remedy Entertainment, it's a little audio trick that makes you hear what you want to hear. In an upcoming interview with GameSpot, audio lead Lucas Pierrot explained that The Board speaks "gibberish," making the character open to interpretation. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f1LEHPr8e_o "An important part of the design is that The Board is basically gibberish, not affiliated to any language," Pierrot said. "So, when you hear a word, you tend to hear what you want to hear … and that’s pretty neat in terms of audio design, as players can fulfill their fantasies. You want to hear The Board praising you for performing an Execution? You can! Maybe you hear them saying 'Absolute cinema, Combo!' et cetera, but if you prefer to think they’re arrogant and only feel disdain for slaying a weak enemy … you can hear that too!" Pierrot explained that The Board has a partial language in place, so players can perceive a sense of intelligence from it. That structure allows The Board to feel "scary, unsettling, or even funny sometimes," and the one rule governing its audio design is "the pulse," a "low, soft kick" to emphasize certain words. "I used this to give weight when necessary to have a nice flow. You can see it as some sort of trick to articulate sentences. It gives rhythm and punctuation," Pierrot added. Following its launch in September, Remedy has continued to fine-tune Control Resonant with updates. gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-moder.excerpt: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now. In keeping with Call of Duty tradition, the day-one DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack , with proceeds going to Activision's charity that supports military veterans find new jobs after they leave the service. The CODE Valor Pack adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character. Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast. Carpenter received the Medal of Honor from President Barack Obama in 2014. At the ceremony, Obama said, "They found Kyle lying face down, directly over the blast area. His helmet was riddled with holes. His gear was melted. Part of his Kevlar vest was blown away. One of the doctors who treated him later said Kyle was, 'Literally wounded from the top of his head to his feet.'" Carpenter underwent brain surgery to remove shrapnel from his head. He had about 40 other surgeries to addresses his injuries, which included a collapsed lung, fractured fingers, and one arm that broke in more than 30 places. He had multiple skin grafts and now has a prosthetic eye, a new jaw, and new teeth. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LtHK15qClkU The Valor Pack includes the Relentless and Valor skins, along with new weapon blueprints, a combat knife, and a weapon charm, among other things. gamespot.com/articles/dead-by-daylight-d.excerpt: Dead by Daylight features dozens of characters, including many licensed heroes and villains from beloved horror franchises, but every once in a while, some of them get delisted. Behaviour Interactive has revealed that Chucky will soon suffer such a fate; he's being delisted on November 24 at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET. Until then, players can grab him and any related cosmetics on sale. Chucky, whose in-game nickname is The Good Guy, debuted in Dead by Daylight in November 2023. Like all characters, he came with three unique perks, all of which will stay in the game after he's gone, Behaviour said. Anyone who has purchased Chucky will retain access to him, as well as any of his alternate skins, like the Tiffany alternate skin voiced by Jennifer Tilly and based on Chucky's wife, Tiffany. For players who own the Chucky DLC, his perks will keep their established names, while anyone who doesn't unlock the DLC before it disappears from all platforms will see his perks change names. You can read those name changes below: Hex: Two Can Play will be called Hex: Eye For An Eye Friends Til the End will be called One Track Mind Batteries Included will be called Gaining Steam Other rewards tied to Chucky, like Prestige rewards and possible quests that allow players to use him, will remain available. "Hi, I'm Chucky. Wanna play? You have one month to unlock access." Behaviour didn't say exactly why Chucky is being delisted. We can assume the rights are expiring, but whether that's simply based on the terms of the original deal or if something changed later on is unknown. gamespot.com/articles/cod-modern-warfare.title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Players Discover A Secret Gun Printer In Multiplayer
gamespot.com/articles/cod-modern-warfare.excerpt: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 players have discovered an Easter egg on one of the multiplayer maps, which is tied to the 3D printer feature found in the DMZ extraction mode. This secret printer lets players grab different gun builds mid-match, and these weapons are fully customized with attachments. As previously discovered by Muggs1213 on Reddit, Modern Warfare 4's Cachette multiplayer map contains one of DMZ's 3D printers. In DMZ, this printer is used to craft essential gear and upgrades specific to the extraction mode, but in multiplayer this device offers random weapon blueprints. https://www.reddit.com/r/modernwarfare4/comments/1xdtc6s/the_map_cachette_has_a_3d_printer_in_the_armory/ Cachette's 3D printer is easily overlooked, especially when you're hot in the action, but it's found upstairs in the map's Armory point-of-interest. There is a weapon inside the 3D printer at the start of each match, and anyone can break the printer case open and retrieve the item inside. So far, players have discovered random weapon builds for guns, such as the Sang 9MM pistol, the PPSH-41 submachine gun, Cronen Squall assault rifle, and the Mosin Nagant marksman rifle. These guns being offered are generally fully kitted five-attachment weapon builds. This printer might only offer random weapon builds, but this is still a fun nod to Modern Warfare 4's DMZ, and it can be helpful to new players who might not have many weapons or attachments unlocked. Modern Warfare 4 launched on October 23, and the game's first DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack , with proceeds going to Activision's charity that helps military veterans find new jobs after they leave the service. If you're just getting started with this new Call of Duty, you may also want to check out our rundown of the best MW4 multiplayer loadouts .
